title: Introduction to Computing Science and Programming I
summary: CMPT 120 introduces programming through small problems, from choosing a loop to debugging a program. SFU designs it for students with little or no programming experience.
questions: If programming was new to you, when did the assignments start to feel manageable?
How much time did you spend debugging compared with writing the first version?

title: Introduction to Psychology I
summary: PSYC 100 looks at how psychologists study questions about perception, learning and motivation. Research design is part of the course alongside the findings themselves.
questions: Did drawing out the research methods help you make sense of the readings?
What mix of reading, recall and practice questions worked for you?

title: General Biology
summary: BISC 101 connects cell biology with how whole organisms work. Lectures and labs explore subjects such as enzymes, genetic information and gas exchange.
questions: How did you spread lab preparation and lecture review across the week?
Which connections between the labs and lectures were worth revisiting before an exam?
